title: Inference Moat Metric: quantifying serving advantage & operational readiness
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Sales, product and exec teams lack a single, quantitative view of Redwood's 'inference moat' — the concrete serving, routing, and ops capabilities buyers cite when choosing us over other providers. Existing artifacts are fragmented (benchmarks, PRDs, ad-hoc research). This ticket will synthesize a repeatable metric ("Inference Moat Score") and an operations-ready signal set that can be surfaced in Console and exported to GTM. The goal is to turn qualitative win-loss themes into measurable signals that drive roadmap prioritization, pricing, and competitive messaging.
proposal_summary: Define a ~10-dimension composite score combining internal telemetry (latency P95, KV cache hit, fallback success rate, real-time autoscale time), product features (private VPC readiness, dedicated capacity lead time, model-variant coverage), market signals (public model availability churn, quantization support), and procurement friction (contract complexity, compliance steps). Build a prototype dashboard in Console (read-only) and a CSV export for Sales. Pilot with 3 enterprise accounts and 1 internal GTM dossier. Deliverables: scoring rubric, data pipelines, dashboard proto, playbook for GTM usage and engineering flags to prioritize mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard spec: formal definition for each dimension, weight, expected value ranges, and normalization method
Data ingestion: ETL queries or metrics definition for each signal (Console metrics, infra telemetry, procurement ticket tags) with daily refresh
Prototype dashboard: Console view showing global leaderboard, per-customer score, and top-3 contributing signals
Export & alerts: CSV export endpoint and one alert rule (score delta > 15% week-over-week) wired to GTM slack channel
Pilot feedback: documented feedback from 3 customers and 2 AE interviews and iteration plan
tasks: PM: finalize dimensions & weighting (owners: PM + Research)
Research: run correlation analysis between historical loss reasons and candidate signals
Eng (Data): implement metrics queries and daily ETL to metrics store
Eng (Console): mock dashboard + visual design handoff
Design: craft visualization and explanatory microcopy for score components
GTM: prepare sales one-pager and 2 demo scripts for pilots
Pilot: onboard 3 enterprise customers and collect structured feedback
Iterate: update weights and surface remediation tickets for high-leverage deficiencies

notes_for_sales: Provide a short narrative and one-pager that maps score ranges to deal motions (e.g., 80+ means low friction for dedicated/private; 50-80 indicates targeted mitigations; <50 requires technical deep-dive). Include 2 demo scripts showing how to use the score in pre-sales calls.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: signals are noisy and may misclassify accounts, leading to GTM mistrust. Mitigation: conservative rollout with manual review for first 6 pilots, clear caveats in one-pager, and feedback loop to adjust weights.
open_questions: What is the canonical customer identifier for joining procurement tickets to telemetry?
Should external public model availability signals be pulled from third-party provider feeds or seeded manually?
Do we expose raw component scores to customers or only the composite?
